1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a Final Fantasy-inspired, turn-based endless-tower RPG with skills, potions, and a merchant between floors.

## Requirements
- Turn-based battles; skills and potions; endless tower progression; merchant between floors.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone responsive browser game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
- Used original “Emberfall — The Endless Spire” fantasy styling and characters.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added playable combat, enemy turns, skills, consumables, leveling, floor progression, sentinel bosses every five floors, merchant purchases, and best-floor tracking.
- Added responsive layout, battle log, action feedback, optional sound toggle, and game-over/retry flow.
- `node --check game.js` passed; Chromium headless DOM rendering completed.

### Active
- Visual and interactive gameplay verification remains to be done.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/emberfall.png` for visual issues.
2. Test combat, victory/shop progression, merchant purchases, game over/retry, and mobile layout in-browser.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game structure and UI.
- `style.css`: Visual design and responsive styling.
- `game.js`: Game state, combat, shop, and progression logic.
- `/tmp/opencode/emberfall.png`: Latest headless Chromium screenshot for inspection.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `playwright-cli` launch failed because its expected Chromium installation was missing; direct `chromium --headless` successfully rendered the page.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8:

10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.

19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

- Turn-based battles, skills, potions, endless tower progression, and a merchant between floors.

- Combat and merchant use modal UI; mobile layout currently stacks the hero panel below the battle panel.

## Objective
- Continue building Emberfall, a mobile-friendly turn-based endless-tower RPG.
- Add merchant status and inventory visibility, a town with purchasable skills, more mythic monsters, and turn-based HP/FP regeneration.

## Requirements
- Keep the merchant scrollable on mobile and show current HP/FP and potion/tonic counts there.
- Add a town outside the tower, with a class specialist who sells skill books the player can buy and learn.
- Structure the town so more NPC types can be added later.
- Give monsters more mythic visual styling.
- Regenerate some HP and FP each turn.

## Decisions
- HP/FP were moved into the battle panel above the arena so they are visible during combat.
- Merchant modal scrolling was updated to support touch scrolling and short screens.
- The town is planned as a separate view reachable from the merchant between floors.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented battle-panel HP/FP display and mobile modal scrolling in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Verified `node --check game.js` passed after those changes.
- Added merchant status markup for HP/FP bars and potion/tonic counts, plus a town navigation button in `index.html`.

### Active
- Wire the merchant HP/FP and inventory markup to game state.
- Implement the town view, extensible NPC rendering, class specialist, skill-book purchases, and learned combat skills.
- Update monster names/visual styling to be more mythic.
- Add HP/FP regeneration each turn.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Complete merchant status rendering and refresh it after purchases.
2. Build the town modal/view and specialist skill-book purchase/learn flow.
3. Add learned skills to combat actions and handle their costs/effects.
4. Add turn regeneration and mythic monster styling.
5. Test battle, merchant, town, purchases, and mobile layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Battle UI, merchant status markup, and planned town UI.
- `game.js`: Game state, combat, merchant behavior, and planned town/skill logic.
- `style.css`: Mobile scrolling, combat vitals, merchant status, town, and monster styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- The new merchant status markup has not yet been connected to `game.js` or styled.

## Objective
- Continue building Emberfall as a mobile-friendly turn-based endless-tower RPG with merchant status, a town skill-book system, mythic monsters, and turn-based regeneration.

## Requirements
- Show current HP/FP and potion/tonic counts on the merchant panel.
- Add a town outside the tower with a class specialist selling skill books the player can buy and learn; keep NPCs extensible.
- Give monsters more mythic visual styling.
- Regenerate HP and FP each turn.

## Decisions
- Keep HP/FP visible in the battle panel above the arena and make merchant dialogs touch-scrollable.
- Skill books are learned immediately upon purchase; learned skills become combat actions.
- Regenerate 2 HP and 1 FP at the end of each enemy turn, subject to resource caps.

## Work State
### Completed
- Wired merchant HP/FP bars and potion/tonic counts to game state.
- Added the Ashen Crossroads town view, extensible NPC rendering, Knight specialist, and purchasable Starfall and Warden’s Aegis skill books.
- Added learned skills to combat actions and implemented their costs and effects.
- Added turn-end HP/FP regeneration and mythic enemy names, ranks, and visual aura styling.
- `node --check game.js` passed; a static check found no missing JS-referenced HTML IDs.

### Active
- Smoke-test battle, merchant purchases, town navigation/skill learning, and responsive layouts in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Browser-test the full battle → merchant → town → skill purchase → next floor flow.
2. Check mobile layouts and adjust any visual or interaction issues.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Battle UI, merchant status, town and skill-book views.
- `game.js`: Game state, combat, regeneration, merchant and town behavior.
- `style.css`: Responsive UI, modal scrolling, town, merchant status, and enemy styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Browser behavior has not yet been verified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Continue building Emberfall as a mobile-friendly turn-based endless-tower RPG with merchant status, town skill books, mythic monsters, and turn-based regeneration.
- Verify the battle → merchant → town → skill purchase → next floor flow and fix responsive layout issues.

## Requirements
- Show current HP/FP and potion/tonic counts on the merchant panel.
- Add a town outside the tower with a class specialist selling skill books the player can buy and learn; keep NPCs extensible.
- Give monsters more mythic visual styling.
- Regenerate HP and FP each turn.
- Keep HP/FP visible in the battle panel above the arena and make merchant dialogs touch-scrollable.

## Decisions
- Skill books are learned immediately upon purchase; learned skills become combat actions.
- Regenerate 2 HP and 1 FP at the end of each enemy turn, subject to resource caps.

## Work State
### Completed
- Wired merchant HP/FP bars and potion/tonic counts to game state.
- Added Ashen Crossroads, extensible NPC rendering, Knight specialist, and purchasable Starfall and Warden’s Aegis skill books.
- Added learned skills to combat actions, turn-end regeneration, and mythic enemy names, ranks, and aura styling.
- Browser smoke-tested floor 1 victory, merchant status, town visit, Warden’s Aegis purchase, return to merchant, and progression to floor 2; the learned skill appeared as a combat action.

### Active
- Fix mobile horizontal overflow: at 390×844, document width was 431px; a temporary CSS override reduced it to 375px and made the header fit.
- Continue mobile checks for battle controls, scrollable merchant/town dialogs, and responsive layouts.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Persist the verified mobile header CSS adjustment in `style.css` and confirm there is no horizontal overflow at phone widths.
2. Test mobile merchant and town scrolling/layout, then capture and inspect screenshots.
3. Re-run checks; note the browser reported a missing `/favicon.ico` (404).

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Battle UI, merchant status, town and skill-book views.
- `game.js`: Game state, combat, regeneration, merchant and town behavior.
- `style.css`: Responsive UI, modal scrolling, town, merchant status, and enemy styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- `node --check game.js` passed; static check found no missing JS-referenced HTML IDs.
- The mobile CSS improvement was only injected in the browser for verification; it has not yet been saved to `style.css`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Continue building Emberfall and fix the merchant display so purchased potion/tonic counts and current HP/FP stay synchronized with game state.

## Requirements
- “The potions and tonics doesn't update the owned amount when I buy a new one from merchant window and the HP and FP shows 40/40 instead of the real data from the current value”
- Preserve the existing battle → merchant → town → skill purchase → next floor flow and mobile-friendly layouts.

## Decisions
- Skill books are learned immediately on purchase and become combat actions.
- Regenerate 2 HP and 1 FP at the end of each enemy turn, subject to resource caps.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added merchant HP/FP bars and supply counts, Ashen Crossroads with a Knight specialist and skill books, mythic enemy styling, and turn-end regeneration.
- Browser-tested floor progression, town visit, skill purchase, and learned combat skill.
- Persisted responsive header adjustments; verified no horizontal overflow at 390×844, 360×800, 320×568, and 280×700.
- Verified merchant and town dialogs scroll at 320×568; added inline favicon; browser console had no errors or warnings.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Investigate and fix merchant state refresh after buying potions/tonics and incorrect HP/FP values.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect merchant purchase handlers and status-render/update functions in `game.js`; trace whether purchases update inventory and refresh merchant UI.
2. Ensure displayed HP/FP uses current player HP/FP and maxima, and potion/tonic counts refresh immediately after purchase.
3. Re-test merchant purchases and HP/FP display in browser, including opening merchant after combat.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, merchant purchase logic, and UI updates.
- `index.html`: Merchant status and supply-count elements.
- `style.css`: Merchant panel and responsive dialog styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Mobile screenshots: `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-merchant-mobile.png` and `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-town-mobile-top.png`.
- The last browser check showed the merchant status at 78/100 HP and 40/40 FP, but the user reports FP incorrectly stays at 40/40 and purchased supply counts do not update.

- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- The latest merchant browser check showed purchased counts updating and merchant HP/FP reflecting current values (including `30 / 40` FP).

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete Emberfall’s mobile-friendly combat presentation with a visible player combatant and Final Fantasy 1-style command menus.
- Add a beginning-of-run choice between Knight, Mage, and Archer, each with distinct skills, stats, visuals, and attack animations.

## Requirements
- Preserve the battle → merchant → town → skill purchase → next floor flow and responsive layouts.
- Purchased skill books are learned immediately and become combat actions.
- Regenerate 2 HP and 1 FP at the end of each enemy turn, subject to resource caps.

## Decisions
- Use Fight, Skills, Items, and Guard command categories.
- Give each class distinct starter skills and stats; tailor town skill-book access to the chosen class.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added class profiles, class skills, class-aware town specialist logic, and dynamic skill action rendering in `game.js`.
- Added class selection, player combatant, in-arena command menu, `#floatLayer`, `#potionCost`, and `#etherCost` hooks in `index.html`.
- Wired class selection, class-specific and learned skill actions, command filtering, and attack animations in `game.js`.
- Preserved end-of-enemy-turn HP/FP regeneration.
- Previously ran `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` successfully.

### Active
- Create `combat.css` for the overlaid menu, visible player fighter, class visuals, attack animations, class-selection screen, and responsive layouts.
- Correct Knight selection copy: it currently says “Crescent Slash · Warden’s Aegis,” but the starter skills are `crescent` and `riposte`.
- Browser-test class selection, combat, progression, merchant/town flows, and mobile layouts.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `combat.css` and align its selectors with `index.html` and `game.js`.
2. Update the Knight class-selection copy to “Crescent Slash · Riposte.”
3. Run syntax/diff checks and browser-test combat, progression, and narrow-screen layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, class profiles, combat actions, town skill books, and progression.
- `index.html`: Class-selection dialog, player combatant, command menu, and combat DOM hooks.
- `style.css`: Existing app styles and responsive layouts for `combat.css` to complement.

## Important Context
- Repository files remain untracked and uncommitted.
- `index.html` references `combat.css`, but that file does not yet exist.
- Class-specific starter skills are Knight: `crescent` and `riposte`; Mage: `ember` and `mend`; Archer: `aimed` and `volley`.

## Objective
- Complete Emberfall’s mobile-friendly combat presentation and beginning-of-run choice among Knight, Mage, and Archer.
- Verify combat, progression, merchant/town skill purchases, and narrow-screen layouts in a browser.

## Requirements
- Preserve the battle → merchant → town → skill purchase → next floor flow and responsive layouts.
- Purchased skill books are learned immediately and become combat actions.
- Regenerate 2 HP and 1 FP at the end of each enemy turn, subject to resource caps.

## Decisions
- Use Fight, Skills, Items, and Guard command categories.
- Give each class distinct starter skills and stats; tailor town skill-book access to the chosen class.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added class profiles, class skills, class-aware town specialist logic, and dynamic skill action rendering.
- Added class selection, player combatant, in-arena command menu, combat DOM hooks, class-specific attack animations, and end-of-enemy-turn HP/FP regeneration.
- Added `combat.css` for combat presentation, class visuals, animations, class selection, and responsive styling.
- Verified Mage selection, Skills menu, Ember Burst combat action, and end-of-turn regeneration in browser; the log showed `+2 HP, +1 FP`.
- Defeated the first enemy and verified the merchant modal opens with victory rewards.

### Active
- Test town skill-book purchase, immediate skill availability, and progression to the next floor.
- Inspect and verify narrow-screen layouts and remaining combat command categories.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. At `http://localhost:3002`, use the current merchant state to visit town and purchase the Mage skill book.
2. Verify the learned skill appears in combat, then return to the merchant and continue to floor 2.
3. Inspect the layout at narrow-screen sizes, address any issues found, and rerun `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, classes, combat actions, town skill books, and progression.
- `index.html`: Class-selection dialog, player combatant, command menu, and combat DOM hooks.
- `combat.css`: Combat scene, command menu, class visuals, animations, and responsive styling.
- `style.css`: Existing app styles and base layouts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status`.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed before the latest browser checks.
- Browser is open at `http://localhost:3002` with the Mage run at the merchant modal; current gold is 43, enough for Mage’s `Starfall` book (38).
- At viewport width 390, `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` was 375; no horizontal overflow was observed.

## Objective
- Complete Emberfall’s mobile-friendly combat presentation and beginning-of-run choice among Knight, Mage, and Archer.
- Verify combat, progression, town skill purchases, command categories, and narrow-screen layouts.

## Requirements
- Preserve the battle → merchant → town → skill purchase → next floor flow and responsive layouts.
- Purchased skill books are learned immediately and become combat actions.
- Regenerate 2 HP and 1 FP at the end of each enemy turn, subject to resource caps.

## Decisions
- Use Fight, Skills, Items, and Guard command categories.
- Give each class distinct starter skills and stats; tailor town skill-book access to the chosen class.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added class profiles, class skills, class-aware town skill access, class selection, combat presentation, animations, and end-of-enemy-turn regeneration.
- Verified Mage’s Ember Burst defeated the first enemy; the log showed `+2 HP, +1 FP`, and victory opened the merchant.
- Purchased Mage’s Starfall book for 38 gold; it was marked learned and appeared in the Skills menu.
- Continued to floor 02; HP/FP were restored to caps and the learned Starfall action is available in combat.
- At viewport width 390, document width was 375 with no horizontal overflow.

### Active
- Inspect narrow-screen usability and verify remaining command categories.
- Consider improving mobile command-tab touch targets: at 390px viewport, tabs measured approximately 39×26px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test Fight, Items, and Guard on floor 02 and verify their combat behavior.
2. Check narrow layouts, including command-menu fit and touch targets; adjust `combat.css` if needed.
3. Rerun `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, class profiles, combat actions, town skill books, and progression.
- `index.html`: Class-selection dialog, combatant, command menu, and combat DOM hooks.
- `combat.css`: Combat presentation, animations, class visuals, and responsive styling.
- `style.css`: Base app styles and layouts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status`.
- Browser is at `http://localhost:3002` with a Mage run on floor 02, 5 gold, Starfall learned, and the enemy alive.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed before the latest browser checks.

## Objective
- Complete Emberfall’s mobile-friendly combat presentation and beginning-of-run choice among Knight, Mage, and Archer.
- Verify combat, progression, town skill purchases, command categories, and narrow-screen layouts.

## Requirements
- Preserve the battle → merchant → town → skill purchase → next floor flow and responsive layouts.
- Purchased skill books are learned immediately and become combat actions.
- Regenerate 2 HP and 1 FP at the end of each enemy turn, subject to resource caps.

## Decisions
- Use Fight, Skills, Items, and Guard command categories.
- Give each class distinct starter skills and stats; tailor town skill-book access to the chosen class.
- Improve mobile command-tab touch height to 44px.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added class profiles, class skills, class-aware town skill access, class selection, combat presentation, animations, and end-of-enemy-turn regeneration.
- Verified Mage’s Ember Burst defeated the first enemy; the log showed `+2 HP, +1 FP`, and victory opened the merchant.
- Purchased Mage’s Starfall book for 38 gold; it was marked learned and appeared in the Skills menu.
- Continued to floor 02; HP/FP were restored to caps and Starfall was available in combat.
- Verified Guard reduces the next enemy hit and Items exposes a usable potion when injured.
- Increased mobile command-tab height from 26px to 44px; no horizontal document overflow at viewport width 390.

### Active
- Test Fight behavior and verify narrow-screen command-menu fit and touch-target widths.
- Rerun JavaScript and whitespace checks after the latest CSS edits.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test Fight on the current run and confirm the enemy turn resolves as expected.
2. Check menu width and touch targets at 390px and narrower widths; tabs are still only about 30px wide in the current layout.
3. Run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game state, class profiles, combat actions, town skill books, and progression.
- `index.html`: Class-selection dialog, combatant, command menu, and combat DOM hooks.
- `combat.css`: Combat presentation, animations, class visuals, and responsive styling.
- `style.css`: Base app styles and layouts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in `git status`.
- Browser is at `http://localhost:3002` with a fresh Mage run on floor 01 after reload; the earlier floor-02 run and learned Starfall are no longer in browser state.
- `combat.css` now sets mobile command tabs to `min-height: 44px` and the small-screen battle menu to `max-height: 58%`; current tab widths measure about 30px.
